chapter: Booker T. Washington Community Center Band
title: Turnover of players and girls joining the marching band
summary: Good readers were taken by big bands each year and replaced; girls aged ten to thirteen came in, played clarinet and trumpet and marched, and nobody objected.

bands.name: Booker T. Washington Community Center Band

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the horn: first instrument and the trombone

blocks.x: So they would take out two or three of the best men.
This year, then some more would come up, see?
More would join the band. It was like a turnover. Then before I left the band, we had girls in there. We had nice girls, you know, playing trumpet, and about five playing clarinets, you know.
Wasn't that kind of unusual? Didn't the families think that was kind of funny, when the girls wanted to play instruments?
Well, I don't know. We never gave it a thought, you know. All at once we looked up, and here they

come, starting with girls. So you didn't ask no questions, you know, because you're getting all this free training, and you were getting the instruments and stuff, you know. A lot of people -- like anything else, a lot of people didn't think too much of it, you know, but the overall, the -- of the band itself, because a lot of people didn't care for her because they tried to say that she was a truant officer and she would take your kid away from you and all that. Well, you know, all those kinds of things. I remember them saying that, and I remember my mother and them talking about it, you know. And I didn't butt into nothing then, you know, a youngster. I was brought up like that. You never -- you say back and listened, you know.
So whatever happened, you know, went along with the deal.
So about the girls, nobody said a word, and they got so they were in the marching band. They'd march right with us, you know, and travel with us. Sure. See they'd --
Sure, 11, 12, you know. Maybe 10, you know.
